output.title: Skin-irritation tag cluster — consistent with open adhesive-lift mechanism (KI-AD-007), no new firmware or magnitude signal
output.summary: The skin-irritation tag co-occurs almost exclusively with adhesion and comfort-fit tags in both current and prior feedback windows, describing patches lifting during high-intensity wear with associated redness/heat. Telemetry shows adhesion_flag rate essentially flat between windows ({f_1} vs {f_2}) and skin_temp_delta_c actually slightly lower in the current window ({f_3} vs {f_4}), with no firmware-version split showing a rate-ratio interval excluding one ({f_5}). This pattern matches the already-open, unresolved adhesive-lift mechanism (KI-AD-007 / KI-UK-008) described in the knowledge base rather than a new hardware, firmware, or app-driven spike. Per support playbook guidance, such clusters must not be waved away as 'expected' and still require an operations-side lot check even absent a statistically distinguishable new signal.

leading_hypothesis.statement: Skin-irritation reports in this window are a continuation of the known, still-open adhesive-lift mechanism (high motion intensity combined with elevated patch-site temperature delta), not a new firmware- or app-specific defect.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: A specific firmware version is driving increased adhesion/skin-irritation flags.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: compare_versions on adhesion_flag across firmware pairs current vs prior; the pair examined showed no rate-ratio interval excluding one

alternative_hypotheses.statement: A new bad adhesive lot (hardware defect) is causing a fresh, distinct spike similar to a prior confirmed lot incident.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: Pull device/lot identifiers for the affected users and check for lot concentration versus the broader population, as was done for the prior confirmed lot incident

alternative_hypotheses.statement: Elevated skin temperature delta alone (independent of adhesion) is driving irritation reports.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: skin_temp_delta_c telemetry actually decreased slightly current vs prior, working against a rising-heat explanation

Knowledge base explicitly describes an open, uncontained adhesive-lift mechanism (high motion intensity plus elevated skin temp delta) matching the described symptoms, distinct from the prior lot-recall incident which was already closed and contained.
Support playbook instructs that adhesion/skin-irritation clusters must not be closed as expected and require escalation to operations for a lot check even when matching the known open mechanism.

counter_evidence.claim: adhesion_flag telemetry rate is essentially unchanged between prior and current windows, showing no meaningful spike.

output.title: Rising claims-interpretation ticket cluster: readiness score misread as clinical/diagnostic result
output.summary: Support/feedback tickets tagged claims-interpretation rose sharply between the prior and current windows and are concentrated in text describing the readiness score as a medical/diagnostic result rather than a wellness indication. The pattern spans multiple firmware versions, app versions, and regions rather than clustering on one build, and closely resembles a previously closed communications incident (INC-2025-002) that was confirmed as a labeling/copy issue rather than a device or sensor defect. Existing policy (KD-05) already prohibits the confused phrasing, but the current ticket volume suggests the on-screen copy or surrounding UI context is still producing this misread among some users despite the recent policy revision.

leading_hypothesis.statement: The rise in claims-interpretation tickets reflects a recurring communications/UI-copy issue in which wearers read the readiness score as a clinical/diagnostic result, consistent with the prior confirmed comms incident INC-2025-002 and the prohibited-description list in KD-05, rather than any change in device behavior across the affected firmware/app versions.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: A firmware or sensor defect is producing anomalous readiness-adjacent outputs that wearers are reasonably interpreting as clinical, i.e. a device-side data quality regression rather than a pure copy/comms problem.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: Compare motion_intensity or related readiness-input telemetry across firmware_version and app_version for the current vs prior window; if no version-specific anomaly appears despite the ticket spread across firmware 1.2.0 through 1.4.2 and app 3.0 through 3.2, a device-side cause is unsupported.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: The spike is a regional or channel-specific artifact (e.g. one market's app store review culture) rather than a broad claims-interpretation problem.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: Tabulate ticket region and channel distribution for the current window; the sampled records already span iberia, nordics, uk, benelux, and dach across beta_forum, app_store_review, and support_ticket channels, which argues against a single-region or single-channel artifact, but a full breakdown would confirm.

deterministic_findings.label: current-window claims-interpretation tickets also tagged data-accuracy

supporting_evidence.claim: Sampled current-window tickets explicitly describe the readiness score being read as a health verdict, lab result, or clinical finding, matching the exact prohibited phrasing categories in KD-05.

Ticket volume grew roughly tenfold between prior and current windows while spanning firmware 1.2.0 through 1.4.2 and app versions 3.0 through 3.2, indicating a copy/comms pattern rather than a version-localized defect.

A near-identical historical incident, readiness screenshots read as clinical results, was closed as a confirmed communications incident, not a device incident, with a KD-05 policy update issued and no scoring code rollback.

KD-05 explicitly prohibits describing readiness as a diagnosis, test result, or condition-detection tool, and instructs support staff to restate the score as a wellness indication rather than argue medicine.

counter_evidence.claim: Some current-window tickets show the intended framing already working correctly, e.g. a wearer confirming the score is wellness only and not a diagnosis, indicating the confusion is not universal even within the tagged set.

recommended_actions.description: Route open claims-interpretation tickets through the KD-03 claims-misread staff script; ensure support does not confirm or deny a medical state and restates the score as a wellness indication only.

Escalate the current ticket volume to Regulatory Communications/Legal to review whether on-screen copy near the readiness score, including label placement and adjacent wording, needs a further revision beyond the recent KD-05 update, given tickets continued to rise afterward.
Do not treat this as a firmware or sensor defect pending further telemetry review; avoid any production code change until a UI-copy root cause review is complete.

uncertainty: No breakdown of ticket region, channel, or firmware counts was retrieved beyond the small sample returned per window, so the claim that the spread is broad rather than concentrated rests on a limited sample.

It is not confirmed whether the specific on-screen copy changed between the prior and current windows; KD-05 was recently revised inside the prior window, so the causal link between that revision and the current-window spike is not established.
No telemetry, such as readiness-input metrics, was checked to fully rule out a concurrent device-side anomaly; this is inferred from firmware and app version spread rather than directly tested.

output.title: Overheating tag cluster traced to cosmetic app battery-chrome UX debt and known Nordics cold-weather drain characteristic, not a thermal defect
output.summary: Feedback tagged 'overheating' in both current and prior windows is concentrated in the Nordics region and, on inspection, describes fast battery drain in cold weather and an alarming red battery-warning screen in the companion app, not device heat. Skin-temp-delta telemetry (the only thermal channel available) shows no elevated or rising signal in the current window and no firmware-linked shift. The pattern matches two standing, closed knowledge-base entries: KI-NW-014 (Nordics cold-weather battery drain, accepted regional characteristic present across firmware trains) and KI-UI-011 (app battery chrome reading as 'overheating', standing cosmetic UX debt). A near-identical ticket cluster was previously investigated and closed as not-an-incident.

leading_hypothesis.statement: The overheating tag reflects a cosmetic app UI element (red battery chrome shown below a battery-percentage threshold, KI-UI-011) co-occurring with a known regional cold-weather battery drain characteristic (KI-NW-014) in Nordics users, rather than an actual thermal event in the device.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: Devices are genuinely overheating and this is a new thermal defect.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: Compare skin_temp_delta_c current vs prior and across firmware/region; if rate is flat or falling and within documented normal range with no firmware-linked step, a genuine thermal defect is not supported.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: A recent firmware or app release introduced a thermal regression that produced these tickets.
alternative_hypotheses.falsifying_test: Compare skin_temp_delta_c rate between the newest and an older firmware version in the current window; a ratio near one with an interval including one indicates no firmware-linked change.

deterministic_findings.label: skin_temp_delta_c rate ratio, firmware 1.4.2 vs 1.3.0, current window

supporting_evidence.claim: Every sampled 'overheating'-tagged feedback record co-occurs with 'battery' and 'app-ui' tags and describes cold-weather battery drain or an alarming app battery screen, not device heat.

The same co-tagging pattern and text content were present in the prior window at a nearly identical volume ({f_4} prior vs {f_3} current records), consistent with a standing characteristic rather than a new or worsening event.
Skin-temp-delta telemetry, the only available thermal proxy, is essentially flat between prior and current windows and shows no firmware-linked shift, arguing against an emerging thermal defect.
Nordics shows an elevated battery_drain_pct versus UK consistent with the magnitude recorded in the standing known-issue register (KI-NW-014).

KI-UI-011 documents that app battery chrome reads as 'overheating' due to a harsh red fill shown below a battery-percentage threshold, a standing cosmetic UX issue present in all regions, matching the ticket content observed here.
KI-NW-014 documents Nordics elevated daily battery drain as an accepted, benign regional characteristic present across firmware trains, not introduced by the latest firmware.
A near-identical Nordics winter drain ticket cluster was previously investigated and closed as not an incident.

counter_evidence.claim: The candidate is flagged as SAFETY_ADJACENT by triage classification, which independently of this investigation's findings still bears a duty of caution around thermal complaints.
